what_it_does: Brain-implant biomedical sensors (EEG electrodes, nerve recording) must listen for tiny electrical signals (50-60 nanovolts per root-hertz, incredibly faint) but survive massive artifacts when a surgeon delivers stimulation pulses (100+ millivolts, a million times larger). Traditional amplifier-first designs saturate and take seconds to recover. This work flips the approach: go straight to analog-to-digital conversion using a delta amplifier in the first stage. The delta amplifier improves the noise-versus-dynamic-range tradeoff by distributing gain across two paths, achieving faint-signal sensitivity while handling huge artifacts instantly.
